issues.description: Static method name mismatch for accepting supply deliveries in SealSaloon: the problem statement UML and descriptive text refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) (see problem_statement.md), and the provided Main example calls shop.acceptSupplyDelivery(...) (template Main.java). The solution implementation instead defines a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) in SealSaloon (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java). Because callers and the specification expect acceptSupplyDelivery, the different identifier in the solution will cause compilation/runtime failures for code that calls acceptSupplyDelivery and will confuse students mapping requirements to implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery with the signature public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) so it matches the UML, problem description, and example Main. Alternatively, if the preferred name is receiveDelivery, update the problem statement UML and example Main to call receiveDelivery instead and ensure tests and descriptions use the same identifier.

issues.description: Contradictory instructions about SealSaloon.stock initialization and mutability: one place in the problem statement instructs that both attributes (orders and stock) "should be initialized to default values (e.g., an empty array or a new object of the class Stock) in the constructor of SealSaloon" (problem_statement.md), implying instance initialization in the constructor. Elsewhere the problem explicitly requires that the stock attribute be static and final (shared across instances) and that some related methods be static (problem_statement.md). These instructions conflict about where/how to initialize the shared static stock and may confuse students about whether to declare and initialize stock as an instance field in the constructor or as a static field at declaration.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement to remove the contradiction: explicitly state that stock must be declared as a static final field (shared across all SealSaloon instances) and should be initialized either at the declaration site or in a static initializer, while the orders array is an instance field that should be initialized in the constructor. Update the sentence that currently instructs initializing "both" attributes in the constructor to specify only the instance attribute (orders) is initialized there.
